key_insight: Entity recognition—not knowledge recall—is the main bottleneck, and distinctive visual clues help VLMs identify entities better than general scene descriptions.
engineering_relevance: Training VLMs to seek entity-specific visual clues can improve recognition and downstream reasoning without injecting new entity knowledge.
method: Identify entity-recall clues: distinctive visual details linked to an entity, such as Saint Peter’s keys.
Extend GRPO with an advantage localized to the entity-recall clue in the thinking trace.
Train on entity recognition to encourage clue-seeking behavior that transfers to other tasks.
evidence_signal: Across four models on ViQuAE, misrecognition caused 76.3% of errors; ClueRL outperformed GRPO and a perception-reward baseline on three recognition benchmarks and improved Qwen3.5-4B by 4.4 and 4.0 points on MMStar’s ScienceQA and MMMU subsets.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify how clue spans are identified or supervised, leaving the implementation cost of localized rewards unclear.
paper_title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
